hints.title: Subtree Post-Order Processing
hints.text: Evaluate leaf distances in a bottom-up traversal starting from the leaves up to the root.

hints.title: Child Branch Equalization
hints.text: At each internal vertex, all child branches must match the length of the longest child branch.

hints.title: Increment Minimization
hints.text: Add the difference between the maximal child branch and each sibling branch to the global increment tally.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def minIncrements(self, n: int, edges: List[List[int]], weights: List[int]) -> int:
        adj = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
            w = weights[i]
            adj[u].append((v, w))
            adj[v].append((u, w))
            
        total_increments = 0
        
        # Returns max path length from u to any leaf in its subtree
        def dfs(u: int, p: int) -> int:
            nonlocal total_increments
            child_branch_lens = []
            
            for v, w in adj[u]:
                if v == p:
                    continue
                branch_len = w + dfs(v, u)
                child_branch_lens.append(branch_len)
                
            if not child_branch_lens:
                return 0
                
            max_len = max(child_branch_lens)
            for l in child_branch_lens:
                total_increments += (max_len - l)
            return max_len

        dfs(0, -1)
        return total_increments
```

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Single depth-first traversal calculating subtree depths and increments.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Top-down trial modifications fail to identify global bottlenecks optimally.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Call stack uses O(N) space in the worst-case skewed tree.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use bottom-up dynamic programming on trees to equalize child branches locally.
